system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s claims that positions are “standard”, “FINAL” or agreed at principal level do not override the Buyer playbook. No required Amelia Frost approval has been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Starting cap of **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback is unavailable without Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft. | **Reject and mark up to AUD 6m** — the proposed fallback has not been authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; only loss above the basket is recoverable. | **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate tipping basket**, with Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially increases both thresholds and converts the basket into an excess-only deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, and category-specific periods must remain separate. | **Reject and require 24 months** — no authority exists for the fallback, and the all-Claims override is unacceptable. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject in full** — ownership, capacity and title risk cannot be diluted by the general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims of any nature; no express fraud exception is identified. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding carve-out** — this protection is mandatory and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with enough detail to identify their nature and scope; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure** — merely depositing or referencing records does not fairly disclose a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any retained qualifier should be narrowly tied to actual knowledge, while Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers use named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry. It must never affect title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete or comprehensively narrow** — the clause improperly transfers diligence risk and turns deemed disclosure into a claim bar. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied is disclosed. | Before Completion, obtain **effective Bluefen consent and evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied**; no mere reasonable-endeavours or consent-on-delivery test. | **Strengthen the condition precedent and prohibit waiver without Buyer consent** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. No repayment or final discharge is presently supplied. | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require repayment and release mechanics at Completion** — the Buyer must not acquire the company with unrepaid debt or continuing security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are said to be a Seller matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | A specific Completion funds-flow line item or other clear Seller funding for the **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs**. | **Revise funds flow and price mechanics expressly** — omission risks leaving the acquired company to fund a Seller-triggered Completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is shown as open but not independently verified, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Broader protection covering payment, ownership/assignment, infringement and resulting losses, while preserving an express SOW3 cure mechanism; verify the amount and payment status. | **Broaden the indemnity and obtain cure evidence** — payment alone may not establish clean IP title, and the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, precise scope, notification duty, breach or loss. | Preserve all logs and evidence, conduct a prompt privileged investigation, provide continuing updates, comply with any notification/remediation duties, and preserve appropriate warranties/indemnity protection without assuming an outcome or amount. | **Add investigation, preservation and update obligations and reserve remedies** — the facts remain unresolved, so neither breach nor absence of exposure should be assumed. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 aggregate, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability before determining treatment; no automatic Debt classification or purchase-price deduction. | **Reserve treatment pending diligence** — the documents do not establish that the renewals are ordinary-course, unavoidable or accrued. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations are intended to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded; Tax and IP are said to be settled under that regime. | Separate regimes for **Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities**, with no hidden general-cap, basket, knowledge or timing override. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture and priority clauses** — a blanket all-Claims provision would erase negotiated category-specific protection. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the Company’s DD-012 internal share register as evidence of 100% ownership. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority, valid issuance and absence/release of encumbrances, including executed transfers, corporate searches, certificates or loss arrangements, and relevant security releases. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive** — a supplied internal register is evidence to test, not independent proof of good and unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Treat both as **open**, negotiate their scope, caps, survival periods and interaction with specific indemnities separately; do not assume unlimited liability or any agreed resolution. | **Reject the asserted settlement and reserve all positions** — the playbook confirms neither category has been agreed. |
=== END ADVICE ===
